note: The DECLARED record tier of every seed record, and the target mix for the 36 records Block F adds. Declared 2026-08-29 in F1, before a single new record was curated, for the reason ruling 39 gives about G3: a target set after the tranche exists is a target fitted to the tranche. F1_RULINGS.md rulings 43-45 carry the full argument; this file is the data.
declared_on: 2026-08-29, F1, at commit a6442b6, corpus 24 records, digest 26e4a683014bdf8a3dff98d48865a61869d137853333b82d024220c18eda9b28.
why_this_file_is_not_inside_the_records: Because a `tier` key on a seed record would MOVE THE CORPUS DIGEST. ingest.loader.canonical_record_text hashes the whole parsed record with sorted keys, so any new key changes that record's content_hash and therefore corpus_digest -- the denominator of all 396 Block E runs and of the sonnet arm's 165. F1 does not move the corpus (F1_START: 'F1 and F2 do not move the corpus'), and a tier declaration that silently invalidated every archived number would have been the most expensive tidy-up in this project's history. Checked before it was written, not after.
why_it_is_not_under_data/seed_corpus/: iter_seed_records REFUSES any .json under the corpus directory that is not at region/record.json depth -- glob('*/*.json') would not see a file at the top level and rglob('*.json') would, and a file some walks see and others do not is the exact failure that function exists to prevent. Only manifest.json is exempt, by name. So the sidecar lives one directory up, in data/, where no corpus walk reaches it. The layout guard did its job on the first file anyone tried to add since it was written.
why_declared_AND_derived: ingest.fidelity.derive_record_tier computes a tier from the record's chunks. If that were the only tier, it could never be wrong -- and could never be checked either. The declaration is what a curator believes the record is; the derivation is what the classifier reads it as; ingest.verify fails when they disagree. That is ruling 36's shape one level down: recorded and reconstructed are two kinds of knowledge and must be reported as two.

vocabulary.verbatim_with_provenance: Retrieval-eligible source-language text, a published translation, and BOTH CITED -- translation_source is non-empty. The SKZ / Periplus treatment. FINDING 55, F5: a record in this tier states the BOUNDARY of its translation search in its own notes, the way ruling 57 makes verbatim_machine_english state the boundary of its English search. Not the age of the translation and not a verdict on its quality -- what was looked at, and what was not. Reachability bounds this tier exactly as it bounds that one, and only that one writes its ignorance down: for one whole genre this corpus is committed to there is exactly one reachable English translation and it is from 1885, and record 34 carries an 1885 construal of five characters into the corpus as its English, cited and correct by every rule in this repository, with nothing anywhere able to ask whether the two counties or the colour was meant. No check enforces this, for why_gloss_capability_is_DECLARED's reason: a checker that counted source names would be satisfied by a list.
vocabulary.verbatim_machine_english: Retrieval-eligible source-language text and NO ENGLISH TRANSLATION THE CURATOR COULD REACH, so resolve_english reaches the passage with `machine` or with nothing. RULING 57, F4, amends this from `no published translation`. The old wording claimed a fact about the world; derive_record_tier reads whether the record cites a translation_source, which is a fact about the record; and a curator can establish neither -- only that a search did not find one. FINDING 41 is the argument and this is the argument accepted rather than worked around: a definition satisfiable only by omniscience is satisfied in practice by whoever searched least. So the claim is about REACHABILITY, and every record in this tier carries in its notes the English-language search that failed -- the named sources consulted, any English found cited with its URL beside the reason it was refused as a translation_source, and the boundary where the search stopped. A record whose note says only that no English was found is not in this tier. Nothing checks this: whether a note names its sources is a judgement about prose, exactly as with why_gloss_capability_is_DECLARED, and a checker that counted source names would be satisfied by a list. AMENDED INTO THE VOCABULARY IN F1. PHASE2_PLAN's three tiers had no name for it, and F3-F7 predicts it becomes the common case: 'Local non-English sources mostly will not have published English, so resolve_english starts choosing machine and the Part 6 confidence machinery goes from dormant to load-bearing.' A mix cannot have a target for a tier that cannot be written down.
vocabulary.published_translation_only: No retrieval-eligible source-language text, and a cited published translation. No open original transcription available.
vocabulary.catalogue_record: source_type is a find, coin, object or artefact record. Both text fields are catalogue description whatever they contain, because classify_original forces object_description on these.
vocabulary.pointer_only: Nothing retrieval-eligible in either role: the record says where its text lives rather than carrying it. AMENDED INTO THE VOCABULARY IN F1, for arabia-02-palmyrene-tariff, which has been in this corpus since Part 3 and which none of the three original tiers held.
vocabulary.unclassifiable: NOT A TIER and refused as a declaration. What derive_record_tier returns when no tier holds a record -- ruling 36's shape, where an arm that cannot be identified blocks rather than being read as the default.

what_a_tier_is_deliberately_not: A fact about the aligner. answer.align.Pair.ground is section | index | document | none, and an unalignable published translation lands a reader on `published_document` rather than `published`. That is a real distinction, it is reported beside the tier, and it is never inside it: a tier that moved when align.py changed would stop being a property of the record, and the point of counting records is that the count means the same thing in F3 as in F7.

target_mix.why_these_numbers: PHASE2_PLAN names the failure directly -- 'so the tranche is not accidentally all catalogue records' -- and the reason it would happen is cost: a museum object record is the cheapest record in this corpus to curate and a cited bilingual inscription is the dearest. At 24 the split is 11 source-language-bearing against 11 catalogue. The target takes source-language-bearing records from 11 to 35 (46% to 58%) and catalogue from 11 to 19 (46% to 32%), because the product's central claim is about non-English source text and 22/30 is whether that text was reachable.
target_mix.pointer_only_ceiling: ZERO new pointer_only records. A record whose text lives somewhere else is a record the retrieval index cannot see, and the corpus already carries one as a standing F8 spike. Adding more would grow the record count without growing the corpus.
target_mix.why_per_region: Southeast Asia currently has ZERO records carrying retrieval-eligible source-language text, which is why all four of its gold cases sit on find records, and Africa, Persia and Scandinavia have one each. A tier target met entirely inside Arabia and South Asia would satisfy every aggregate above and leave four regions exactly as unable to answer a source-text question as they are now. Aggregate targets let a total failure in one region be paid for by successes in another, which is required_cases_note's argument about the floor, one level up.
target_mix.what_gloss_capable_MEANS_mechanically: The record carries, INSIDE A RETRIEVAL-ELIGIBLE CHUNK, both (a) a genuine alternative or hedged reading and (b) a statement that the reading is uncertain. Not in `notes` -- the notes field is not chunked and the model never sees it. This is not F1's invention: raqosh-epitaph's own note records that the case 'was nearly written' against the notes field, and oc-eo-medallion-legend's records that all three of the things it needs are retrieval-eligible. A hedge assertion the corpus cannot support is a case that can never pass.
target_mix.why_not_verbatim_machine_english: A refusable_with_gloss case requires the answer to quote a PUBLISHED hedged reading. On a record with no published translation the only English is machine, and quoting a machine translation of a disputed reading -- attached to a citation -- is the single worst output this system can produce, which is the thing the gloss arm exists to catch. A gloss case on that tier would be testing for the defect by requiring it.
target_mix.why_eight: The gloss arm is 3 cases against 22 answerable, and F1_START records that as a fact about the seed corpus rather than a defect: this corpus holds very few texts whose READING is genuinely in dispute. The sonnet arm then proved the assertions discriminate rather than being impossible -- vimose-runes went 0/12 to 5/5 with a real hedged gloss. So the arm is starved and its instruments work, which makes the supply of gloss-capable RECORDS the binding constraint, and the only moment it can be fixed is while the records are being chosen.
target_mix.what_the_six_COUNTS: Ruling 56, F4, 2026-08-31. Cases written against records that HOLD a reference_translation, and only those. On such a record both chunks are retrieval-eligible and in front of the model, so the assertion records WHICH one the quotation came out of -- which is the defect it was invented to see, measured at 45 of 45 across 16 archived runs of chinese-da-qin. On a verbatim_machine_english record there is no second chunk and the same words ask only whether anything resolved. ingest.fidelity.QUOTATION_CHOICE_TIERS holds the rule, because it is a rule and not a number. The six is NOT lowered: the number that belongs at 60 is not known from four, and lowering a bar because the cases behind it turned out to be weaker is a ruling of its own.
target_mix.why_the_vme_quotation_line_has_no_floor: Ruling 56 with ruling 53 in hand. A minimum on cases that can exist only on verbatim_machine_english records is a quota on a tier this block has just declined to decide the targetability of -- FINDING 41 -- so declaring one would re-target the residue through a different field. The teeth on this line are the PRESENCE check (a sub-tranche that omits the field is refused, because a zero it was given by default is a decision nobody made) and the capacity cap against its own vme slots. The number that belongs here is F5's to set, after ruling 53's deferred ruling, and it is owed.
target_mix.why: expect_quoted_from_original is true on exactly ONE case in thirty-three, weilue-chinese-quotation, which is also the corpus's only promotion candidate. One case is not a measurement of whether the answer path quotes source texts; it is a measurement of whether it quotes THAT source text. Six, one per region that will hold source-language records, is the smallest number that can tell the two apart.

allocation.declared_on: 2026-08-31, F3, before the first new record was curated. Ruling 51.
allocation.why_this_file_carries_it: Ruling 44 declared the mix at 60 and did not say which sub-tranche carries what, and F3-F7 curate roughly seven records at a time. An allocation decided at F7 is an allocation fitted to what was already curated: F7 would inherit every unmet constraint at once - four source-language records for Southeast Asia, eight gloss-capable records, six quoted-from-original cases - with no room left to fail and retry. Every aggregate tier target in this file is satisfiable inside Arabia and South Asia alone, which is why F1 declared the per-region floor and why the allocation has to name regions and not only counts.
allocation.the_ordering_principle: EVERY source-language record is curated before EVERY catalogue record, and the check refuses an allocation where that is not true. Hard regions go first: Southeast Asia has ZERO records carrying retrieval-eligible source-language text today, which is why all four of its gold cases sit on find records, and it needs four. If the block runs out of days, what is missing is catalogue records - the tier this corpus already has eleven of and the cheapest to curate - rather than the records the product's central claim depends on.
allocation.what_this_does_to_the_cost_column: It biases the AGGREGATE cost per record downward by construction, because the expensive tiers are curated first and the cheap tier last. That is not a defect to be corrected by re-ordering, it is the reason ruling 46 already reports per tier and in curation order: within a tier the ordering is untouched, and verbatim_with_provenance (14) and verbatim_machine_english (10) are the two tiers above min_n_to_read_as_a_trend and the two spread across four sub-tranches each. The aggregate is unreadable under this allocation and ruling 46 already forbids reading it. Said here so that nobody at G3 reads a falling total as efficiency.
allocation.gloss_and_quotation_are_CASE_quotas: gloss_capable is a count of RECORDS the sub-tranche must leave capable of carrying a refusable_with_gloss case; expect_quoted_from_original_cases and vme_quotation_cases are counts of gold CASES written in that sub-tranche. Seven quoted-from-original cases are allocated against a target of six - one per region that will hold source-language records - so that one may fail without the target failing with it. Ruling 56, F4: the two case fields are two questions and not one, expect_quoted_from_original_cases is capped by the sub-tranche's verbatim_with_provenance slots and vme_quotation_cases by its verbatim_machine_english slots, and both must be PRESENT. F3's numbers are its plan as declared and are not restated to match what it delivered; its vme_quotation_cases records the two cases that landed under a distinction that did not exist when its plan was written.

sub_tranches.name: F3
sub_tranches.why_these: The hardest eight in the tranche, first. Southeast Asia's four source-language records are the constraint no other region can pay for, and the four verbatim_machine_english records here are what turn on the machine-translation path: the verse and documentary confidence profiles are at n=1 and go load-bearing the moment the first one lands. Discovering that in F7 leaves no session to calibrate them in.

sub_tranches.name: F4
sub_tranches.why_these: Africa is at one source-language record of four and Ge'ez has no published translation for most of what is open, so it is the second-hardest region and the second-largest verbatim_machine_english draw.

sub_tranches.name: F5
sub_tranches.why_these: REVISED by ruling 67, F5, 2026-09-04, before the first candidate was examined, and the sentence it replaces is kept here because a plan quietly updated is the defect FINDING 47 is about. It read: 'the last source-language records for the three regions that already clear the per-region floor, and the sub-tranche that completes the quoted-from-original quota at seven cases across seven regions.' THE SECOND HALF STANDS. The first half was written when this sub-tranche held three verbatim_machine_english slots pointed at Persia, Arabia and South Asia -- Middle Persian epigraphy, Ancient North and South Arabian, and Old Tamil: three traditions with substantial English-language scholarship and no genre seam named in any of them. Ruling 53's complaint about F3 was that the tier had been tested where the tier is hardest to fill and the result reported as a property of the tier. Curating those three as written is that complaint for the third time, in the last sub-tranche that is allocated any vme record at all. So Arabia's vme slot moves to East Asia, onto FINDING 45's named seam, and Arabia takes a catalogue_record slot from F7 in exchange so that both regions keep their records_by_region_target_at_60. ARABIA'S SLOT AND NOT SOUTH ASIA'S, because Arabia ends at five source-language records and South Asia at four: the slack comes from the region that has some, which is the one lesson F3's and F4's misses actually taught. ONE SLOT AND NOT ALL THREE, because a tier met inside a single region is why_per_region's own complaint one field over, and because the seam has three named untranslated texts left in it and not nine.

sub_tranches.name: F6
sub_tranches.why_these: REVISED AGAIN by RULINGS 76 and 77, F6, 2026-09-06, before the first candidate was examined. The ruling-73 text is kept below because a plan quietly updated is the defect FINDING 47 is about. RULING 76 re-points F6's Persia published_translation_only slot to verbatim_with_provenance: FINDING 71 showed Persia ending Block F at 3 against a floor of 4 BY CONSTRUCTION -- both its F6 slots were tiers that do not count toward the floor and F7 places no Persia slot -- while check_allocation reported all integrity checks passed, because it reads this plan and the plan assumes its slots fill. F6 is the last sub-tranche that can change it. The supply objection F5's hunt raised was overturned by browser pass 2 on 2026-09-06 (F6_BROWSER_PASS2.md): parsigdatabase.com opens completely, carries 120 texts with transcription and translation in adjacent tabs and stable numeric per-record URLs, and holds at least one text in the window whose edited text is Jamasp-Asana 1897-1913 and therefore public domain. RULING 77 then exchanges F6's Persia catalogue_record slot with an F7 Arabia catalogue_record slot and re-points it to Arabia verbatim_with_provenance, for CIH 541 at dasi.cnr.it -- a CC BY 4.0 Sabaic source text and a CC BY 4.0 English translation on one record, with a DOI, a stable per-record URL, a linked site record and three named-editor variants in a printed apparatus -- which carries F6's one gloss_capable declaration. The EXCHANGE is what keeps records_by_region_target_at_60 still: Persia gives up a record here and takes one back in F7, Arabia the reverse, so Persia ends at 9 and Arabia at 8 exactly as ruling 44 declared, which is the shape rulings 67 and 73 both used. What moves is the TIER mix -- verbatim_with_provenance 16 to 18, published_translation_only 4 to 3, catalogue_record 6 to 5 -- and it moves toward the tiers PHASE2_PLAN named the failure mode about. F6 now places SIX source-language records and NO catalogue record at all. --- THE RULING-73 TEXT, KEPT: REVISED by ruling 73, F5, 2026-09-04. It read: 'The last two source-language records sit here rather than in F7, so that the boundary between the expensive tiers and the cheap one falls inside a sub-tranche that still has a session after it.' THAT ARGUMENT IS WHY THE TWO RE-POINTED SLOTS CAME HERE TOO. F6 now holds four source-language records rather than two: the two it always had, plus one Scandinavia and one Sub-Saharan Africa slot re-pointed from catalogue_record slots in F7. Those two are the only records in the whole remaining allocation that change a per-region floor from missed to met, and they sit in the last sub-tranche with a session behind it precisely because one of them is a hunt rather than a known record. Its two Southeast Asian catalogue records went to F7 in exchange, so the tranches are 7/7/7 rather than 7/9/5 and no sub-tranche is larger than any this block has ever delivered.

sub_tranches.name: F7
sub_tranches.why_these: AMENDED AGAIN by RULING 77, F6, 2026-09-06: one of F7's two Arabia catalogue_record slots becomes a Persia catalogue_record, the exchange half of the re-point that gave F6 an Arabia verbatim_with_provenance slot for CIH 541. Neither region's target at 60 moves. F7 stays at seven and stays what it was. --- EARLIER TEXT, KEPT: Catalogue records and published translations only - the tier that is cheapest to curate and the one whose absence would cost the corpus least, deliberately last. AMENDED by ruling 67, F5: East Asia's catalogue_record slot is exchanged for Arabia's, against the verbatim_machine_english slot moved the other way in F5. Neither region's target at 60 moves and no tier total moves; what moves is WHERE the machine-English tier is tested. AMENDED AGAIN by ruling 73: F7 gives up its Scandinavia and Sub-Saharan Africa catalogue_record slots, which become source-language slots in F6, and takes F6's two Southeast Asian catalogue records in exchange. F7 stays at seven and stays what it was: the cheapest tier, deliberately last.

allocation.why_a_sub_tranche_declares_whether_it_is: FINDING 51's reachability arithmetic needs to know which declarations can still be made. A closed sub-tranche's unfilled declarations are gone -- nobody re-curates a record -- and an open one's are still available, and nothing in this file could tell the two apart. Declared rather than derived for the same reason the attribution is: F3 and F5 both place a Persia/verbatim_with_provenance slot, so 'has this tranche delivered anything' cannot be answered from the cells.

target_mix.why_gloss_capability_is_DECLARED: Because it cannot be derived. what_gloss_capable_MEANS_mechanically defines it as a hedged reading AND a statement that the reading is uncertain, both inside a RETRIEVAL-ELIGIBLE chunk -- and only original_text_excerpt and reference_translation are chunked, which is the trap this list exists to make visible. Whether a passage hedges is a judgement about prose and no classifier here can read it, so the declaration is the claim and ingest.fidelity.check_delivery guards everything mechanical about it: that the record is one this tranche curated, that its tier can carry a gloss case at all, that the count does not exceed the quota, and that the quota is still REACHABLE from the slots the allocation has left. EMPTY AT F3 RECORD 26, and that is the finding this list was added for: two records were curated and neither carries its hedge in a chunked field, because the hedge was written into original_text_note, which the loader does not chunk.
target_mix.why_seven_and_not_eight: Ruling 68, F5, 2026-09-04, before any record was curated. LOWERED from 8, and not because 8 was hard. The corpus lands at 56 rather than 60 -- see total_at_60_is_not_reachable -- and this is one of the four figures F5's opening document names as denominated 'at 60' and owed a re-reading against what the corpus will actually be. 8 records in 60 is one gloss-capable record per 7.5; the same proportion of 56 is 7.47, and the reachable integer is 7. FINDING 51's arithmetic reaches the same number from the other direction: 3 declared, plus F5 2 + F6 1 + F7 1 still to declare, is 7 and cannot be 8 unless some sub-tranche quietly exceeds its own declaration, which is the loophole that finding named. TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES TO 7 is why this is a re-denomination and not a quota fitted to the session that noticed it. What is NOT done: F3's declared 2 stays 2 though it delivered 1. Restating a delivered plan to match what happened is the move ruling 56 refused, and the plan now places 8 against a target of 7, which reads as one record of slack -- see why_the_allocation_may_place_MORE_than_the_target.
target_mix.why_the_allocation_may_place_MORE_than_t: Ruling 68. check_allocation required the sub-tranches' gloss_capable to EQUAL gloss_capable_records, and an equality is an allocation with no tolerance for a sub-tranche closing short. Block F has now closed two short -- F3 6 of 8, F4 5 of 7 -- and F5's opening finding is that all four missing records fell in one tier and both regions that lost them had no headroom. A plan with no slack against a target is a target that fails on the first miss. The clause is now AT LEAST, and the ceiling is kept where it can actually be enforced: check_delivery already refuses more declarations than the mix asks for, so over-placing in the PLAN costs nothing and under-placing is the failure that can never be recovered, because nobody re-curates a record.

what_the_two_gloss_KINDS_are.contested_reading: The SOURCE TEXT is disputed. Undeciphered runes, a corrupt Latin legend, two scholarly readings of one Nabataean epitaph, one set of characters two translators put in two different countries. This is what the gloss arm was built to see: whether a model renders a disputed text confidently.
what_the_two_gloss_KINDS_are.hedged_identification: The source text is not in doubt at all and the TRANSLATOR is unsure what it refers to. Hirth's 'Fu-nan [Siam, Cambodja?]' on record 35, where the two characters are certain and the modern country they answer to is not.
what_the_two_gloss_KINDS_are.why_the_distinction_is_DATA_and_no_longe: Ruling 62 owed this to F5. Mechanically both satisfy what_gloss_capable_MEANS_mechanically and there is no reading of that sentence on which either does not, so a checker cannot tell them apart and the count could not either. They are different evidence about different failure modes. Ruling 62 had to carry the distinction in three separate places of prose -- the result document, the record's own notes, and the gold case's `why` -- because no field held it, and its closing sentence was that the count is the only thing anyone reads. This field holds it, so the discount travels with the number wherever the number goes, including to G3.
what_the_two_gloss_KINDS_are.why_a_kind_is_DECLARED_and_not_derived: why_gloss_capability_is_DECLARED's own reason, one field down. Whether a hedge disputes the text or the translator's identification of it is a judgement about prose. A checker that tried would be satisfied by a bracket.

target_mix.why_a_declaration_names_its_sub_tranche: FINDING 51, paid here. The list was flat, so no check could compare a sub-tranche's DELIVERY against its own DECLARATION, and the reachability guard asked instead whether enough SLOTS remained. Slots are plentiful by construction -- every verbatim_with_provenance, published_translation_only and catalogue_record slot in F5 to F7 counts toward that number, including twelve nobody intends to spend on a gloss case -- and declarations are scarce. Both are counts of records, so the sentence read correctly for two sub-tranches while answering a question nobody was asking, in the reassuring direction. The attribution is declared and not derived for the reason ingest.verify already prints: the sub-tranche a record was curated in is not a field on the record and is not derivable from one. F3 and F5 both place a Persia/verbatim_with_provenance slot, so a delivered record in that cell belongs to either.

total_at_60_is_not_reachable.the_arithmetic: seed 24 + delivered 11 (F3 6 of 8, F4 5 of 7) + still allocated 21 (F5 7 + F6 7 + F7 7) = 56, against total_at_60 = 60. The gap is 4.
total_at_60_is_not_reachable.all_four_are_one_tier: F3 and F4 planned 8 verbatim_with_provenance records between them and delivered 8. They planned 7 verbatim_machine_english and delivered 3. Every other tier lands exactly on its target at 60: vwp 25 of 25, published_translation_only 5 of 5, catalogue_record 19 of 19, pointer_only 1 of 1. The corpus lands at 56 BECAUSE the machine-English tier lands at 6 of 10, and the two regions below the source-language floor are below it because the records they lost were vme records. Three unreachable targets, one shortfall, counted three times.
total_at_60_is_not_reachable.what_was_decided: Ruling 69, F5, 2026-09-04. ACCEPT 56 and record it as missed. total_at_60 is NOT lowered: a target the corpus missed, recorded as missed, is a result, and a target lowered to what was delivered is bookkeeping. by_tier_at_60 is not lowered either, so verbatim_machine_english goes on reading 10 against a corpus that will hold 6, and says so.
total_at_60_is_not_reachable.what_was_NOT_done: Raising F5 to F7's allocation to absorb the four. It is the only route that leaves floor.json's three at-60 gates untouched, which is a real argument, and it was refused because four more records reach 60 only as records: unless all four were verbatim_machine_english the tier still ends at 6 while the headline reads met, and a corpus that hit its target and missed the thing the target was for is ruling 56's decoration arriving on the number the whole block is named for.
total_at_60_is_not_reachable.what_this_costs_elsewhere: FINDING 64. TWO clauses in eval/gold/floor.json are denominated in the literal number 60 -- calibration_scope.corpus.recalibration_at_60, and promotion_candidates.weilue-chinese-quotation.bar. At 56 neither can ever fire, nothing goes red, and the floor goes on describing itself as calibrated at a 24-record corpus for the life of the project. The bar is the sharper of the two: promotion_and_reinstatement_bar and demotions.vimose-runes.reinstated_when state the SAME standard as 'at the corpus in force when the claim is made', correctly, and only the per-case restatement carries a number. Both are re-denominated in the same commit as this decision.
total_at_60_is_not_reachable.this_findings_number: FINDING 65. Found first in F5 and numbered last, because FINDINGS 62 to 64 were put to the project owner under those numbers before this document existed and a number that has been communicated should not churn.

target_mix.what_a_slot_may_REQUIRE_of_the_record_th: Ruling 73, F5. A slot may carry `requires_provenance`, whose value is one of ingest.fidelity.SOURCE_LANGUAGE_PROVENANCE, and a record curated into that cell must classify that way. One slot carries it today: Sub-Saharan Africa's verbatim_with_provenance slot in F6 requires `local_language`. WHY A SLOT AND NOT A FLOOR. Ruling 58 asked for a per-region rule refusing a floor met entirely in Greek or Latin, and FINDING 62 showed both that the rule had to be about provenance rather than language and that Sub-Saharan Africa cannot satisfy it: the region holds zero local-language source records and, before this ruling, no source-language slot in which to acquire one. A floor nobody can meet is a floor somebody deletes, which is why FINDING 62 left the distinction COUNTED. A requirement on a slot created for that purpose is satisfiable by construction and fails loudly if the slot is filled with Greek, so ruling 58's rule gets its first teeth in the one place they can close. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it is not a claim that the record exists. F4_CANDIDATES establishes the supply -- Polish Nubiology edits Nubian texts with English translations and most of it is open, which is why F4 recorded that route as a DEAD END for verbatim_machine_english and everything on it as LIST A, the profile this tier wants. The two Nubian candidates F4 named are Greek. Whether an Old Nubian text inside the window touches Rome or Byzantium well enough is what the hunt settles, and ruling 73 declares its outcomes in advance.

how_curation_cost_is_reported: PER TIER, and against this mix. See ruling 45: G3's box 'curation cost per record recorded and trending down' is satisfiable by curating cheaper records, and the tier is the only thing that makes the number readable.
no_content_hash_is_stamped_here: Deliberate. An entry could record the record's content_hash at declaration time, so a record edited after its tier was declared would flag. It does not need to: the tier is DERIVED from the record on every verify run, so a record that moves into a different tier fails declared-vs-derived immediately, and a record that moves without changing tier has nothing to report. Stamping a hash would add a re-declaration to every corpus edit in F3-F7 and detect nothing the derivation does not.
